criteria.criterion: For both the bash and powershell tools, pwsh and powershell accept only the pinned literal -Command/-c form after the allowed pre-options, judge every remaining word joined with spaces as a powershell call, preserve the phase and root, and count each wrapper toward the eight-level nesting limit.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/expand.go:202-208 refuses expanded policy values; internal/fence/judge.go:324-334 recurses in the PowerShell mode while preserving the Judge and incrementing depth; internal/fence/wrappers_test.go:10-45 and 83-109 exercise both outer tools, phase/root and the depth limit.

criteria.criterion: Missing, expanded, encoded, file, stdin, bare-script and unsupported-option pwsh forms fail closed with the exact W1 reasons, including the wrapper's written pwsh or powershell name where specified.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/expand.go:173-233 enforces the pinned options and exact refusals, and internal/fence/wrappers_test.go:21-41 asserts the named missing, expanded, encoded, file, stdin, bare-script and unsupported-option cases for both outer tools.

criteria.criterion: cmd accepts only /c or /k after /d, /q and /s, judges its literal string split at &, &&, || and |, and denies % or ^; every other cmd form fails closed with the exact W1 reason.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/expand.go:235-268 validates the wrapper form and special characters; internal/fence/judge.go:272-287 applies splitCMD and the cmd-specific lexer; internal/fence/wrappers_test.go:50-81 covers the accepted options/operators and refused forms in both outer tools.

criteria.criterion: A command inside a wrapper is allowed or denied exactly as the same command in the wrapped tool would be, including case-insensitive command and option matching and names with a path or .exe.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/split.go:300-310 makes every parenthesis literal in syntaxCMD, so cmd /c "(git push)" becomes a command named "(git" and is allowed, although cmd executes the grouped git push command and a direct git push is denied. This leaves a wrapper bypass contrary to the criterion.

criteria.criterion: Committed Go tests cover the allowed and refused wrapper forms, option and name variants, command matching, nesting, phase/root preservation and both outer tools, and the go check executes them.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/wrappers_test.go covers the listed behavior and variants for bash and powershell, and .vloop/tmp/checks.json records the go check exiting 0 with internal/fence passing in its log.

findings.summary: The cmd-specific lexer treats parentheses as literal words, allowing cmd /c "(git push)" even though cmd executes the grouped command and the direct git push command is denied.

notes: Fail closed or correctly judge cmd command groups; add a committed regression test comparing the grouped wrapper with direct git push.
